Standard Errors of Fitted Category Probabilities by the Delta Method for the Nested Logit Model

John Fox

2023-05-20

Source: vignettes/standard-errors.Rmd
standard-errors.Rmd

This document uses the delta method (Fox, 2021, sec. 6.3.5) to derive approximations to the variances of estimated probabilities for dichotomous logit models, and from these, for the nested logit model. The standard errors of these estimated probabilities are the square-roots of their respective variances.

Notation

Let ψj\psi_j represent the probability that the dichotomous response in the jjth nested dichotomous logit model is Yj=1Y_j = 1 (i.e., a “success”), j=1,…,m−1j = 1, \ldots, m - 1, where mm is the number of response categories for the polytomy. Then 1−ψj1 - \psi_j is the probability that Yj=0Y_j = 0 (i.e., a “failure”). I assume that the regression coefficients and their covariance matrix for each dichotomous logit model are estimated in the usual manner.

Let λj=log[ψj/(1−ψj]\lambda_j = \log[\psi_j/(1 - \psi_j] represent the (estimated) logit (log-odds) for the jjth dichotomous logit model, with variance V(λj)V(\lambda_j) (see below).

Let ϕk\phi_k, k=1,…,mk = 1, \ldots, m represent the probability that the polytomous response is Y=kY = k.

Let ψ̂j\widehat{\psi}_{j} and ϕ̂k\widehat{\phi}_k represent the estimates of these probabilities.

In the sequel, which involves only the estimates of these and other parameters, I’ll omit the hats so as to simplify the notation.

In the nested logit model, the polytomous probabilities ϕk\phi_k are each products of probabilities ψj\psi_j or 1−ψj1 - \psi_j for j∈ℳk⊆{1,…,m−1}j \in \mathcal{M}_k \subseteq \left\{ 1, \ldots, m - 1 \right\}; that is ℳk\mathcal{M}_k is the subset of the dichotomous logit models that enter into ϕk\phi_k. Let ψj,kj\psi_{j, k_j} represent either ψj\psi_j or 1−ψj1 - \psi_j, as appropriate for category kk of the polytomous response. Then ϕk=∏j∈ℳkψj,kj\begin{equation*} \phi_k = \prod_{j \in \mathcal{M}_k} \psi_{j,k_j} \end{equation*} for k=1,…,mk = 1, \ldots, m.

Finally, the individual-category probabilities ϕk\phi_k can be converted into logits, Λk=log[ϕk/(1−ϕk)]\Lambda_k = \log[\phi_k/(1 - \phi_k)]. The estimates of these logits should approach asymptotic normality more rapidly than the estimates of the corresponding probabilities.

An Example

I’ll use the following example to illustrate the results in this document: Suppose that we have a three-category response variable YY with categories AA, BB, and CC, and define the two nested dichotomies Y1Y_1 coded 0 or 1 for categories {A}\{A\} and {B,C}\{B, C\}, respectively, and Y2Y_2 coded 0 and 1 for categories {B}\{B\} and {C}\{C\}. Then ψ1=Pr(Y1=1)=Pr({B,C})\psi_1 = \Pr(Y_1 = 1) = \Pr(\{B, C\}); 1−ψ1=Pr(Y1=0)=Pr({A})1 - \psi_1 = \Pr(Y_1 = 0) = \Pr(\{A\}). As well, ℳA={1}\mathcal{M}_A = \{1\} and ℳB=ℳC={1,2}\mathcal{M}_B = \mathcal{M}_C = \{1, 2\}. Consequently, ϕA=ψ1,A1=1−ψ1ϕB=ψ1,B1ψ2,B2=ψ1(1−ψ2)ϕC=ψ1,C1ψ2,C2=ψ1ψ2\begin{align*} \phi_A &= \psi_{1, A_1} = 1 - \psi_{1}\\ \phi_B &= \psi_{1, B_1}\psi_{2, B_2} = \psi_{1}(1 - \psi_{2}) \\ \phi_C &= \psi_{1, C_1}\psi_{2, C_2} = \psi_{1}\psi_{2} \end{align*} Here, I abuse the notation slightly in the interest of clarity, using letters rather than numbers for the response categories, so the index of response categories, kk, takes on the values AA, BB, and CC, rather than 1, 2, and 3.

Variances of the Estimated Probabilities

For the Dichotomous Logit Models

The estimated probability of success ψj\psi_{j} for the jjth dichotomous logit model is ψj=11+e−λj\begin{equation*} \psi_{j} = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\lambda_{j}}} \end{equation*} Then λj=α(j)+β1(j)x1+⋯+βp(j)xp=𝐱T𝛃(j)\begin{align*} \lambda_{j} &= \alpha^{(j)} + \beta_1^{(j)} x_1 + \cdots + \beta_p^{(j)} x_p \\ &= \mathbf{x}^T \boldsymbol{\beta}^{(j)} \end{align*} is a function of the regression coefficients, where 𝐱T=[1,x1,…,xp]\mathbf{x}^T = [1, x_1, \ldots, x_p] (an arbitrary vector of values of the regressors) and 𝛃(j)=[α(j),β1(j),…,βp(j)]T\boldsymbol{\beta}^{(j)} = [\alpha^{(j)}, \beta_1^{(j)}, \ldots, \beta_p^{(j)}]^T. The probability of failure is 1−ψj=11+eλj\begin{equation*} 1 - \psi_{j} = \frac{1}{1 + e^{\lambda_{j}}} \end{equation*} The variance of the logit is V(λj)=𝐱TV(𝛃(j))𝐱V(\lambda_{j}) = \mathbf{x}^T V(\boldsymbol{\beta}^{(j)}) \mathbf{x},

The derivatives of ψj\psi_{j} and 1−ψj1 - \psi_{j} with respect to λj\lambda_{j} are dψjdλj=e−λj(1+e−λj)2d(1−ψj)dλj=−eλj(1+eλj)2\begin{align*} \frac{d\psi_{j}}{d\lambda_{j}} &= \frac{e^{-\lambda_{j}}}{\left( 1 + e^{-\lambda_{j}} \right)^2} \\ \frac{d \left(1 - \psi_{j} \right)}{d\lambda_{j}} &= - \frac{e^{\lambda_{j}}}{\left( 1 + e^{\lambda_{j}} \right)^2} \end{align*}

By the univariate delta method, V(ψj)≈(dψjdλj)2V(λj)=[e−λj(1+e−λj)2]2V(λj)V(1−ψj)≈[d(1−ψj)dλj]2V(λj)=[eλj(1+eλj)2]2V(λj)=V(ψj)\begin{align*} V(\psi_{j}) &\approx \left( \frac{d\psi_{j}}{d\lambda_{j}} \right)^2 V(\lambda_{j}) \\ &= \left[ \frac{e^{-\lambda_{j}}}{\left( 1 + e^{-\lambda_{j}} \right)^2} \right]^2 V(\lambda_{j})\\ V(1 - \psi_{j}) &\approx \left[ \frac{d \left(1 - \psi_{j} \right)}{d\lambda_{j}} \right]^2 V(\lambda_{j}) \\ &= \left[ \frac{e^{\lambda_{j}}}{\left( 1 + e^{\lambda_{j}} \right)^2}\right]^2 V(\lambda_{j}) \\ &= V(\psi_{j}) \end{align*}

For the Nested Logit Model

The variances of the estimated response-category probabilities for the polytomous response can be obtained similarly by the multivariate delta method, recognizing that these probabilities are products of the dichotomous probabilities. The result is greatly simplified because the dichotomies are independent, and so the covariance matrix of the estimated dichotomous probabilities is diagonal.

The required derivatives are ∂ϕk∂ψj,kj=∏j′∈ℳk−{j}ψj′,kj\begin{equation*} \frac{\partial \phi_k}{\partial \psi_{j, k_j} } = \prod_{j' \in \mathcal{M}_k - \{j\}} \psi_{j', k_j} \end{equation*} for j∈ℳkj \in \mathcal{M}_k and k=1,…,mk = 1, \ldots, m. Here, −- denotes set difference. Because V(ψj)=V(1−ψj)V(\psi_{j}) = V(1 - \psi_{j}), it’s always the case that V(ψj,kj)=V(ψj)V(\psi_{j, k_j}) = V(\psi_{j}), and so V(ϕk)≈∑j∈ℳk(∂ϕk∂ψj,kj)2V(ψj)=∑j∈ℳk(∏j′∈ℳk−{j}ψj′,kj)2V(ψj)\begin{align*} V(\phi_k) &\approx \sum_{j \in \mathcal{M}_k} \left( \frac{\partial \phi_k}{\partial \psi_{j, k_j} } \right)^2 V\left( \psi_{j} \right) \\ &= \sum_{j \in \mathcal{M}_k} \left( \prod_{j' \in \mathcal{M}_k - \{j\}} \psi_{j', k_j} \right)^2 V\left( \psi_{j} \right) \end{align*} for k=1,…,mk = 1, \ldots, m.

Applying these results to the example, recall, first, that ℳA={1}\mathcal{M}_A = \{1\} and so the set for the product ∏j′∈ℳA−{j}ϕ(j′,Aj)\prod_{j' \in \mathcal{M}_{A} - \{j\}} \phi^{(j', A_j)}, that is, j′∈{1}−{1}j' \in \{1\}-\{1\}, is empty. In this case, the product is taken = 1, and V(ϕA)=V(ψ1)V(\phi_A) = V(\psi_{1}). That makes intuitive sense, because, as noted previously, ϕA=1−ψ1\phi_A = 1 - \psi_{1}.

Proceeding with BB and CC, ℳB=ℳC={1,2}\mathcal{M}_B = \mathcal{M}_C = \{1, 2\}. Consequently, each product ∏j′∈ℳB−{j}ψj′,Bj\prod_{j' \in \mathcal{M}_{B} - \{j\}} \psi_{j', B_j} and ∏j′∈ℳC−{j}ψj′,Cj\prod_{j' \in \mathcal{M}_{C} - \{j\}} \psi_{j', C_j} has only one term, for j′=2j' = 2 in the case of BB or j′=1j' = 1 in the case of CC: V(ϕB)=ψ2,B2V(ψ1)+ψ1,B1V(ψ2)=(1−ψ2)V(ψ1)+ψ1V(ψ2)V(ϕC)=ψ2,C2V(ψ1)+ψ1,C1V(ψ2)=ψ2V(ψ1)+ψ1V(ψ2)\begin{align*} V(\phi_B) &= \psi_{2, B_2} V(\psi_{1}) + \psi_{1, B_1} V(\psi_{2}) \\ &= (1 - \psi_{2}) V(\psi_{1}) + \psi_{1} V(\psi_{2}) \\ V(\phi_C) &= \psi_{2, C_2} V(\psi_{1}) + \psi_{1, C_1} V(\psi_{2}) \\ &= \psi_{2} V(\psi_{1}) + \psi_{1} V(\psi_{2}) \\ \end{align*}

Yet another application of the delta method produces approximate variances for the individual-category logits. The relevant derivative is dΛkdϕk=1ϕk(1−ϕk)\begin{equation*} \frac{d\Lambda_k}{d\phi_k} = \frac{1}{\phi_k(1 - \phi_k)} \end{equation*} for k=1,…,mk = 1, \ldots, m, and so V(Λk)≈(dΛkdϕk)2V(ϕk)=[1ϕk(1−ϕk)]2V(ϕk)\begin{align*} V(\Lambda_k) &\approx \left( \frac{d\Lambda_k}{d\phi_k} \right)^2 V(\phi_k) \\ &= \left[ \frac{1}{\phi_k(1 - \phi_k)} \right]^2 V(\phi_k) \end{align*}
